QuestionStmt.S: The logical statement $$\sim (\sim p \lor q) \lor (p \land r) \land (\sim q \land r)$$ is equivalent to

Solution.S:
Simplify the given logical expression step by step:

$$\sim (\sim p \lor q) \lor (p \land r) \land (\sim q \land r)$$

Using De Morgan's law: $\sim (\sim p \lor q) = p \land \sim q$.

$$\equiv (p \land \sim q) \lor (p \land r) \land (\sim q \land r)$$

Using distributive law: $p \land (\sim q \lor r)$.

$$\equiv p \land (\sim q \lor r) \land (\sim q \land r)$$

Using associative law: group $\sim q$ terms.

$$\equiv p \land [(\sim q \lor r) \land \sim q] \land r$$

Using absorption law: $(\sim q \lor r) \land \sim q = \sim q$.

$$\equiv p \land \sim q \land r$$

$$\equiv (p \land r) \land \sim q$$

Final Answer: $$\boxed{(p \land r) \land \sim q}$$

Hence, the correct option is A.
